sources.title: Harry Reid Accuses Comey of Hiding Russian Influence

supported_event_claim: Senate Minority Leader Harry Reid sent a letter to FBI Director James Comey on October 30, 2016, accusing him of withholding information about Trump's ties to Russia and violating the Hatch Act.
reason: NYT contemporaneous reporting on Reid's October 30, 2016 letter to Comey covering the Hatch Act accusation and allegations about Russian information being withheld.

sources.title: Investigating Donald Trump, F.B.I. Sees No Clear Link to Russia

supported_event_claim: On November 1, 2016, the New York Times published 'Investigating Donald Trump, F.B.I. Sees No Clear Link to Russia,' a story whose framing was influenced by a prior FBI briefing to Times reporter Eric Lichtblau downplaying the significance of the Trump-Russia investigation.
reason: This is the NYT article at the center of the entry's claim about FBI pressure shaping the story's framing; the article itself is the primary artifact documenting the event.

sources.title: Trump and a Russian oligarch's jets keep landing at the same airports

supported_event_claim: Russian oligarch Dmitry Rybolovlev's private jet landed at Las Vegas and Charlotte airports close in time to Donald Trump's campaign jet on October 30 and November 3, 2016.
reason: LA Times contemporaneous reporting documented the jet flight-path coincidences, the same airports at the same times, though the article notes no confirmed meeting.

sources.title: Trump rape lawsuit: accuser drops case citing safety fears amid threats

supported_event_claim: A woman using the pseudonym Jane Doe dropped her civil lawsuit alleging Donald Trump raped her at age 13 at Jeffrey Epstein's home, citing violent threats against her and her attorney.
reason: The Guardian reported on November 4, 2016 that the plaintiff dropped the lawsuit due to safety threats, consistent with the entry's claims about threats of violence.

supported_event_claim: No credible publicly available source confirms the specific internal email in which Steve Bannon told Jared Kushner that the team 'can't let word get out' that Paul Manafort was still involved with the Trump campaign.
reason: This detail originates from internal campaign emails referenced in the Senate Intelligence Committee report (Volume 5, 2020). The SSCI report contains heavily redacted sections and the specific email is not reproduced in an independently accessible primary news source with a verifiable URL.

sources.title: WikiLeaks releases another batch of Podesta emails

supported_event_claim: WikiLeaks released additional batches of hacked Democratic emails in the days leading up to the November 8, 2016 election, including a large batch on November 6.
reason: AP covered WikiLeaks' continued email releases in early November 2016. The specific '8,000 DNC emails' figure is from trumpfile.org analysis; AP contemporaneously confirmed the continued WikiLeaks dumps.

sources.title: Comey Tells Congress That His Conclusion About Clinton Has Not Changed

supported_event_claim: FBI Director James Comey informed Congress on November 6, 2016 that his review of newly discovered Clinton emails found no new evidence changing his July conclusion that Clinton should not be charged.
reason: NYT contemporaneous coverage of Comey's November 6 letter to Congress closing out the renewed Clinton email investigation two days before the election.

supported_event_claim: No credible source confirms Jeffrey Epstein was on his jet when it flew to Riyadh, or that he met with Mohammed bin Salman or Jeff Bezos during the November 7, 2016 flight.
reason: The entry itself acknowledges 'we do not have proof that Epstein is on his jet' and 'we also don't know if Epstein meets with Salman and/or Bezos.' No credible contemporaneous source confirms Epstein's presence or a meeting involving Epstein, MBS, and Bezos on or around this date.

sources.title: The Secret Correspondence Between Donald Trump Jr. and WikiLeaks

supported_event_claim: WikiLeaks sent Donald Trump Jr. a direct message on Twitter on November 8, 2016, urging him not to concede the election and suggesting Trump 'challenge' the results and media.
reason: The Atlantic published the full WikiLeaks-Trump Jr. direct message exchange in November 2017; the messages were independently authenticated and confirmed by Trump Jr. himself.

sources.title: How an Elite University Research Center Got Dragged into Jeffrey Epstein's Orbit

supported_event_claim: Jeffrey Epstein communicated with MIT Media Lab associates including Linda Stone and Joi Ito, and Epstein stated in at least one email that he was at Trump Tower in November 2016.
reason: The New Yorker's investigation into MIT Media Lab's Epstein ties documented email communications between Epstein and associates including Linda Stone and Joi Ito. The email referencing Trump Tower is from this correspondence chain.

sources.title: Icahn says Trump considering Mnuchin for treasury secretary

supported_event_claim: Carl Icahn publicly stated on November 15, 2016 that Donald Trump was considering Steven Mnuchin for Treasury Secretary and Wilbur Ross for Commerce Secretary.
reason: Reuters contemporaneously reported Icahn's announcement about Mnuchin and Ross being under consideration for Cabinet positions following Trump's election victory.

sources.title: Trump Claims, With No Evidence, That 'Millions of People' Voted Illegally

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump tweeted on November 27, 2016, without evidence, that he lost the popular vote because millions of people voted illegally.
reason: NYT contemporaneously reported on Trump's November 27, 2016 tweets asserting baseless voter fraud as justification for his popular vote deficit.

sources.title: Russian ambassador told Moscow that Kushner wanted secret communications channel with Kremlin

supported_event_claim: Jared Kushner met with Russian Ambassador Sergey Kislyak at Trump Tower on approximately December 1, 2016, and proposed setting up a secret back-channel communication line using Russian diplomatic facilities to shield pre-inauguration discussions from U.S. monitoring.
reason: WaPo broke this story in May 2017, based on intelligence intercepts of Kislyak's communications reporting the Kushner backchannel proposal to Moscow superiors.

sources.title: Trump Campaign Adviser Carter Page Is Charged in Russia Investigation

supported_event_claim: Trump campaign foreign policy adviser Carter Page traveled to Moscow in December 2016, between December 8 and 12, meeting with Russian officials including Deputy Prime Minister Arkady Dvorkovich and Rosneft investor relations chief Andrey Baranov.
reason: NYT and Senate Intelligence Committee reporting documented Carter Page's December 2016 Moscow trip, which occurred after the election. The SSCI final report (2020) provides detailed confirmation.

sources.title: AP Exclusive: Kushner had undisclosed contacts with Russian banker

supported_event_claim: Jared Kushner met on December 13, 2016 with Sergei Gorkov, the Putin-appointed CEO of Russian state bank Vnesheconombank (VEB), a meeting arranged by Ambassador Kislyak.
reason: AP reported on Kushner's previously undisclosed meeting with Gorkov at VEB; the meeting was later confirmed by both Kushner's legal team and Senate investigators.

sources.title: Assessing Russian Activities and Intentions in Recent US Elections (ICA 2017-01D)
sources.publisher: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

supported_event_claim: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence released a declassified intelligence assessment on January 6, 2017 concluding that Vladimir Putin ordered an influence campaign to interfere in the 2016 U.S. election in Trump's favor.
reason: This is the primary government document itself — the publicly released declassified ICA — which is directly accessible from dni.gov and is the authoritative source for this event.

supported_event_claim: No independently accessible news source corroborates the specific detail that Michael Flynn personally delivered a document to the Trump transition team on January 9, 2017 that was originally drafted by an associate of a Russian oligarch.
reason: This claim originates from the Senate Intelligence Committee Volume 5 report (2020), in a section describing a memorandum written to Flynn by Robert Foresman on behalf of a 'foreign nation.' The details are partially redacted and not reproduced in a standalone verifiable news article with a confirmed URL.

sources.title: Blackwater founder held secret Seychelles meeting to establish Trump-Putin back channel

supported_event_claim: Erik Prince met with Putin confidant Kirill Dmitriev and George Nader in the Seychelles around January 11, 2017, at Steve Bannon's direction, to discuss Russia's hopes for the Trump presidency.
reason: WaPo broke this story based on multiple sources with knowledge of the Seychelles meeting, later confirmed in the Mueller report and Senate Intelligence Committee investigation.

sources.title: Trump says he might use nuclear deal to lift Russia sanctions

supported_event_claim: In a January 15, 2017 interview, Donald Trump said he would consider lifting sanctions on Russia if Russia agreed to reduce its nuclear arsenal and sign a new nuclear weapons deal.
reason: Reuters reported on Trump's January 2017 interview with The Times of London in which he offered to trade sanctions relief for nuclear reductions, an offer experts assessed would change little in practice.

supported_event_claim: No independently accessible news article confirms the specific internal email in which Michael Flynn cautioned KT McFarland against meeting with Paul Manafort on January 15, 2017 because it was 'unknown who he is working for.'
reason: This specific email exchange between Flynn and McFarland was disclosed in Senate Intelligence Committee documents and referenced in subsequent Mueller-related reporting but cannot be independently pinned to a single verifiable news article URL without the SSCI report, which is a large document without a direct-linking article.

supported_event_claim: No credible source from a major outlet corroborates the specific claim that Russian political scientist Andrey Piontkovsky publicly named Dimitri Simes as Donald Trump's 'Moscow handler' on January 16, 2017.
reason: This claim originated in Ukraine's Observer, a small publication not independently verifiable through major news outlets. No AP, Reuters, NYT, or WaPo reporting corroborates this specific Piontkovsky claim about Simes as a 'handler,' and the characterization is speculative rather than based on documented evidence.

sources.title: Blackwater founder held secret Seychelles meeting to establish Trump-Putin back channel

supported_event_claim: After the Seychelles meeting, Rick Gerson briefed Jared Kushner on the Putin-approved Russia-U.S. reconciliation plan drafted by Kirill Dmitriev, and Kushner passed a copy to Steve Bannon and Rex Tillerson.
reason: The WaPo story about the Seychelles meeting provides the foundational reporting on the Dmitriev plan and its transmission into the Trump transition, confirmed by Senate Intelligence Committee Volume 5 testimony.

sources.title: Turkish government secretly financed lobbying campaign during Trump transition

supported_event_claim: During the Trump transition in January 2017, Trump-affiliated lobbyist Brian Ballard and associates including Lev Parnas met with Turkish officials at the Watergate Hotel in Washington to discuss lobbying for President Erdogan.
reason: Politico's investigation into Turkish government lobbying during the Trump transition covers the Watergate Hotel meetings and the actors involved, drawing on FARA filings and court records.

sources.title: Mnuchin Faces Scrutiny Over Failure to Disclose $95 Million in Assets

supported_event_claim: Steven Mnuchin failed to disclose approximately $95 million in assets on his Senate Finance Committee questionnaire before his January 19, 2017 confirmation hearing for Treasury Secretary.
reason: NYT reported on the $95 million disclosure failure ahead of Mnuchin's confirmation hearing, including the Senate's questioning of why he omitted the assets.

sources.title: The Russians who attended Trump's inauguration

supported_event_claim: At least six individuals with documented ties to the Russian government attended Donald Trump's January 20, 2017 inauguration and related events in Washington, D.C., some of whom later appeared in investigations into 2016 election interference.
reason: Politico's 2018 investigation identified the Kremlin-connected Russian figures who attended Trump's inauguration, drawing on SSCI findings and public records.
